html:
The Tenino are a Sahaptin speaking people of the Columbia River in north central Oregon, living along the river near The Dalles and up the Deschutes and John Day rivers. Their bands included the Wyam at Celilo Falls and the Tygh.

They fished salmon at the falls, dug roots and traded at the great market of the Wasco and Wishram. Their kin included the Yakama and Umatilla. In 1855 they signed a treaty and moved with the Wasco to the Warm Springs reservation, where they form part of the Confederated Tribes of Warm Springs.
